pr_comments:
I am not sure if it was only my bad luck as just after I installed the current PR and run my first install command:

```
$ ansible-galaxy collection install -U community.general
Starting galaxy collection install process
[WARNING]: Collection at '/Users/ssbarnea/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/foo/bar' does not have a MANIFEST.json file, nor has it galaxy.yml: cannot
detect version.
Process install dependency map
ERROR! Error when getting collection version metadata for community.general:6.3.0 from default (https://galaxy.ansible.com/api/) (HTTP Code: 502, Message: Bad Gateway Code: Unknown)
FAIL: 1
```

Still, I run again few minutes latest and it works, apparently also fast. What I find weird is that I did not see any proof that current implementation did some retries when "502" was returned. Maybe that is not covered by this change.

> ERROR! Error when getting collection version metadata for community.general:6.3.0 from default (https://galaxy.ansible.com/api/) (HTTP Code: 502, Message: Bad Gateway Code: Unknown)

This is not one of the codes that we retry.

> > ERROR! Error when getting collection version metadata for community.general:6.3.0 from default (https://galaxy.ansible.com/api/) (HTTP Code: 502, Message: Bad Gateway Code: Unknown)
> 
> This is not one of the codes that we retry.

After a convo with someone from the galaxy team, I've added 502 as an error code that we will retry.

issue_context.title: Extend use of `retry_with_delays_and_condition` within Galaxy API requests to retry on `TimeoutError`
issue_context.body:
### Summary

As of now, we only retry galaxy API requests when they result in error codes defined within `RETRY_HTTP_ERROR_CODES`.

Some times there are also transient timeout errors, that are not represented by these status codes, and instead raise a `TimeoutError`.

Evaluate extending the function used by `should_retry_error`, to also retry on `TimeoutError`.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
```


### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
```

Out-of-the-scope note:
This leaves an unclosed resource open and should be converted to a CM in a future refactoring.
Note to self: This method needs updated to return `AnsibleError` with `orig_exc`.

```suggestion
from http import HTTPStatus
from http.client import BadStatusLine, IncompleteRead
```

It'd be nice to avoid raising a generic `AnsibleError` from the internal layers. I know that there's some leftovers in here but raising more such non-specific exceptions is only making the matter worse. A `RuntimeError`, which I believe his exception conversion represents, should be more than enough. Although, the exceptions that may happen at this stage are probably related to the initial request/connection (since the consumption is happening later). So maybe a [`ConnectionError`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ConnectionError) would be more accurate.

This exception is raised to the user, so then we'd need to catch a RuntimeError and raise an AnsibleError. I like the current implementation, rather than creating layers and layers of unnecessary exception handling.
Isn't it being converted in `api.py` already? Also, only the outer layer should be interacting with the user, otherwise abstractions leak.

`api.py` does nothing for conversions. For one it's in `module_utils` and doesn't have access to raise `AnsibleError`.

It simply re-raises whatever exception is encountered. 

Unfortunately, we'd have a lot of work to do, to not have leaky abstractions.  As it is, so much of the code base operates under the assumption that all layers raise `AnsibleError` for direct user feedback, and we handle it in the CLI code.  Otherwise, it's just an arbitrary unhandled exception type.  I actually wasn't doing this originally, and we had a bunch of integration tests that started failing.

An exercise for future consideration.

How about
```suggestion
            ) from e
```
Maybe something we can look at in the future. The existing code was of course written before we could really use this, and as such, a lot of things are designed around the `orig_exc` pattern.
